title: लेखनाथ पौडेल र उनको ‘पिंजराको सुगा’ कविताको वस्तुविधान lekhnath Poudel ra Unko "Pinjarako Suga" Kabitako Bastubidhan
authors: विष्ट Bista, सीताराम Sitaram राज Raj
nepali: नेपाली साहित्यमा कवि शिरोमणिबाट विभूषित पौड्याल नेपाली कविताको परिष्कारवादी धाराका प्रारम्भकर्ता हुन् । उनको ‘ऋतुविचार’ (१९७३) बाट यस धाराको प्रारम्भ भएको मानिन्छ । उनमा सुरुमा सल्बलाएको धार्मिक–आध्यात्मिक भावना पछि मानवतावादतर्फ बढेको पाइन्छ । उनमा पूर्वीय सभ्यताप्रतिको असीम श्रद्धा र आर्य सभ्यता संस्कृतिको पुनर्जागरण, समाज सुधारको चाहना, नैतिक उपदेश, प्रकृतिको तन्मय चित्रण आदि प्रवृत्तिहरू पाइन्छन् । प्रस्तुत “पिंजराको सुगा” कविता सममात्रिक पादाकुलक छन्दमा रचना भएको छ । वनकुञ्जको स्वच्छन्द वातावरणमा सयर गर्ने सुगा चरीलाई बन्द पिंजरामा कैद गरिदिँदा उसका वेदनामय भाव नै यस कविताको विषयवस्तु रहेको पाइन्छ । उनको यस कवितालाई अभिधार्थ, प्रतीकार्थ, ध्वन्यार्थ, आध्यात्मिक अर्थ र कवि जीवन सापेक्ष अर्थ गरी विभिन्न तहमा अर्थ लगाउन सकिन्छ । अनि यिनैका आधारमा शीर्षक सार्थकता पहिल्याउन सकिन्छ । प्रथम पुरुषीय आत्मकथनको आत्मालापीय वर्णनगरी रचना भएकाले यसमा प्रथम पुरुष कवि वक्तृप्रौढौक्तिको प्रयोग भएको पाइन्छ ।
american_english: In Nepali literature, Poudyal, adorned with the title Crest-Jewel of Poets, is regarded as the founder of the reformist school of Nepali poetry. This school is considered to have begun with his 'Ritu Vichar' (1973). In him the religious-spiritual feeling that was first stirred is seen to have later grown toward humanism. Such tendencies as boundless reverence for Eastern civilization and the revival of Aryan civilization and culture, the desire for social reform, moral instruction, and the immersed depiction of nature are found in him. The present poem 'Pinjarako Suga' is composed in the pādākulaka metre with even measure. When the parrot-bird, roaming freely in the open air of the forest grove, is imprisoned in a closed cage, its anguished feelings themselves are found to be the subject matter of this poem. This poem of his can be interpreted at various levels by taking it as literal meaning, symbolic meaning, suggested meaning, spiritual meaning, and meaning relative to the poet's life. And on the basis of these very meanings, the meaningfulness of the title can be established. Because it is composed by making a soliloquy-like description of a first-person self-narrative, the use of first-person vaktṛprauḍhokti (the poet-speaker's mature utterance) is found in this.
british_english: In Nepali literature, Poudyal, adorned with the title Crest-Jewel of Poets, is regarded as the pioneer of the school of refinement in Nepali poetry. This school is held to have begun with his 'Ritu Vichar' (1973). In him the religious-spiritual feeling that was first stirred is seen to have later grown towards humanism. Tendencies such as unbounded reverence for Eastern civilisation and the renaissance of Aryan civilisation and culture, the wish for social reform, moral teaching, and the absorbed portrayal of nature are found in him. The present poem 'Pinjarako Suga' is composed in the pādākulaka metre of balanced measure. When the parrot-bird, roaming freely in the open air of the forest grove, is locked in a closed cage, its pained feelings themselves are found to be the subject-matter of this poem. This poem of his may be interpreted at various levels by taking it in terms of literal meaning, symbolic meaning, suggested meaning, spiritual meaning, and meaning relative to the poet's own life. And on the basis of these very meanings, the significance of the title may be established. Since it is constructed through a soliloquy-like account of a first-person self-narrative, the use of first-person vaktṛprauḍhokti (the mature utterance of the poet-speaker) is evident in it.
australian_english: In Nepali literature, Poudyal, decorated with the title Crest-Jewel of Poets, is seen as the originator of the school of poetic refinement. This school is reckoned to have kicked off with his 'Ritu Vichar' (1973). In him the religious-spiritual feeling that got going early on is seen to have later swung towards humanism. You find tendencies in him like limitless reverence for Eastern civilisation and the revival of Aryan civilisation and culture, a longing for social reform, moral instruction, and nature shown in an absorbed sort of way. The present poem 'Pinjarako Suga' is put together in the evenly measured pādākulaka metre. When the parrot-bird, roaming free in the open air of the forest grove, gets shut up in a locked cage, its suffering feelings themselves turn out to be the subject matter of this poem. This poem of his can be read on a number of levels, treating it as literal meaning, symbolic meaning, suggested meaning, spiritual meaning and a meaning tied to the poet's life. And on those very grounds you can establish why the title works. Because it is put together as a soliloquy-style telling of a first-person self-account, the use of first-person vaktṛprauḍhokti (the poet-speaker's assured statement) shows up in it.
informal_english: Right, so in Nepali literature, Poudyal — he carries the title Crest-Jewel of Poets — is the one who founded the reformist school of Nepali poetry. People reckon that school kicked off with his 'Ritu Vichar' (1973). You can see the religious-spiritual mood that first stirred in him swing over towards humanism later on. Then there are all sorts of tendencies in him: endless reverence for Eastern civilisation and reviving Aryan civilisation and culture, wanting social reform, moral teaching, really getting into nature in his imagery — that sort of thing. 'Pinjarako Suga', the poem under discussion, is written in the pādākulaka metre, with even measure. Once the parrot-bird, wandering free in the open air of the forest grove, gets shut up in a locked cage, its poor suffering feelings turn out to be the whole subject of the poem. You can take this poem of his and read it on several different levels — literal, symbolic, suggested, spiritual, and a meaning tied to the poet's own life. And on those very grounds you can work out why the title earns its place. Since it's put together as a sort of soliloquy-style telling of a first-person self-account, you get the use of first-person vaktṛprauḍhokti — the poet-speaker's mature voice — in it.
